tapeLine: Thursday 29 October closed lower on an Alphabet sell-off: S&P 500 -0.3% to 7,720.39, Nasdaq Composite -1.38% to 26,184.72, Dow -132.54 points (-0.25%) to 52,342.56, per search-indexed coverage of the 29 Oct close (Yahoo Finance, CNBC, CNN). Friday futures levels were not confirmed.
matters:
Alphabet Class A closed at $283.82 on Thursday 29 October, down 12.64% and about $499.8 billion of market value, per the Wall Street Journal as cited in search results; the decline was reported as its worst day on record. Coverage tied it to a third-quarter miss on earnings and revenue, negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion, and renewed worry about AI spending.

Microsoft beat estimates but gave up early gains and ended roughly flat, per CNN (29 Oct); sources differed on the exact move, so no figure is carried. Small caps rallied against the index decline, per Benzinga (29 Oct).

Amazon’s company release dated 29 October reports third-quarter net sales up 12% to $201.9 billion and operating income of $28.1 billion (13.9% margin). Its after-hours share reaction was not found.

The S&P 500 closed about 1.2% under its 7,811.54 record close of 9 October, per the prior brief.
